aliases: Observation of the rare decay Bs0 -> mu+ mu- (CMS and LHCb combined)

claim.quote: The combined analysis produces the first observation of the $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay, with a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations, and the best measurement of its branching fraction so far.

date.note: Nature 522 (2015) 68 publication year; the joint preprint arXiv:1411.4413 was submitted on 17 November 2014

name: Observation of the rare decay B⁰ₛ → μ⁺μ⁻ (CMS and LHCb combined)
notes: A joint CMS + LHCb result. collaboration:lhcb is outside this workstream and is not referenced as an id.

significance.quote: a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations

summary.plain: CMS and LHCb pooled their data to see, for the first time, a B meson decaying into two muons - a decay that happens only about three times in a billion.
summary.technical: Joint CMS+LHCb analysis of 7 and 8 TeV data: first observation of B0s -> mu+mu- at >6 sigma, plus 3 sigma evidence for B0 -> mu+mu-; branching fractions compatible with the standard model.

title: Observation of the rare $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay from the combined analysis of CMS and LHCb data
why_it_matters: The decay is strongly suppressed in the standard model, so its rate is one of the sharpest constraints on new heavy particles in flavour physics.
